Conduit, Cable Tray & Industrial Wiring Methods

Electrical path · Free · Plant-floor course outline

On the job

Conduit, Cable Tray & Industrial Wiring Methods is not a hunt for a magic parameter. It is a sequence: isolate energy, verify the print, measure the supply, measure the load, then change one thing. Drive faults, overload trips, and megger readings get faked when someone skips the 10-minute wait or treats a ground fault like an overcurrent. Write the as-found before you clear the fault.

The useful version of Conduit, Cable Tray & Industrial Wiring Methods is the version you can run on nights without a specialist on the radio. Industrial wiring methods including rigid conduit, EMT, cable tray, and tray cable. Covers conduit bending, fill calculations, cable tray fill rules, and NEC Chapter 3 requirements for industrial installations. Keep the as-found. Change one variable. Hand the next crew a log, not a story.

Who it is for

Industrial electricians and techs who live in MCCs, VFDs, and motor leads — not residential work, not HVAC capacitor jobs.

Who it is not for: license mills, VR demos, or anyone looking for a fake testimonial. We do not invent customer quotes. Certificates of completion after quizzes go in the file. They are not a journeyman card, an ISA credential, or NFPA 70E qualification by themselves.

Course outline: 3 modules, 5 lessons, about 3.9 hours

Module 1: Conduit Systems

  • Rigid, EMT & Conduit Bending (50 min)
  • Cable Tray & Tray Cable (45 min)

Module 2: Pulling & NEC Chapter 3

  • Conductor Pulling & NEC Chapter 3 Requirements (45 min)

Module 3: Industrial Wiring Applications

  • Motor Feeders & Branch Circuit Wiring (45 min)
  • Hazardous Area Wiring & Sealing Practices (50 min)

Training is educational. It does not replace your site's lockout/tagout, permits, PPE, or required licenses. Certificates of completion go in the file. They are not a license.
